content: G protein-coupled receptor 119, also referred to as GPR119, is a receptor encoded by the GPR119 gene in humans. It belongs to the family of G protein-coupled receptors and has been identified, along with GPR55 and GPR18, as a potential novel cannabinoid receptor. In both rodents and humans, GPR119 is primarily expressed in the pancreas and the gastrointestinal tract. In rodents, it is also found in the brain. Activation of this receptor has been demonstrated to reduce food intake and limit body weight gain in rats. Furthermore, GPR119 plays a role in regulating the secretion of incretin hormones and insulin. Due to these effects, drugs targeting this receptor are being explored as potential therapeutic options for managing obesity and diabetes. Several endogenous and synthetic ligands that interact with GPR119 have been identified. These include: 2-Oleoylglycerol Anandamide AR-231,453 MBX-2982 Oleoylethanolamide (an endogenous ligand) PSN-375,963 PSN-632,408
